It likely directs the government to fund or conduct research into TB to better understand and fight the disease. Because no official summary is available yet, the exact details of what studies or actions are required are not fully known.
key_provisions: Fund or support tuberculosis research
Honor Shandra Eisenga through named legislation
Potentially improve TB detection or treatment efforts
who_it_affects: This bill would primarily affect people at risk for tuberculosis, medical researchers, and public health agencies responsible for tracking and treating infectious diseases.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in Congress and has been sent to a House committee for review, meaning it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: 21st Century Federal Writers’ Project Act
plain_title: Bringing Back a Government Program to Hire Writers
plain_summary: This bill would create a modern version of the Federal Writers' Project, a 1930s government program that paid writers to create books, guides, and stories during the Great Depression. It would give government funding to writers, authors, and storytellers who need work, similar to how the original program helped thousands of people during hard economic times. Think of it like a government job program, but specifically for creative writers.
key_provisions: Create a new federal program to hire and pay writers
Produce written works that benefit the public, like guides or histories
Model the program after the successful 1930s Federal Writers' Project
who_it_affects: This bill would most directly help writers, authors, poets, and other creative professionals who struggle to find steady work, by giving them government-funded job opportunities.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in the House of Representatives and has been sent to a committee to be reviewed, but has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Protecting Health Care and Lowering Costs Act of 2026
plain_title: Bill to Undo Medicaid Cuts and Work Requirements from 2026
plain_summary: This bill would cancel several recent Medicaid changes that were passed as part of a larger law called the 'One Big Beautiful Bill Act.' Those changes included requiring some Medicaid recipients to work or volunteer to keep their health coverage, and limiting which immigrants can receive Medicaid benefits. By repealing these rules, this bill would restore Medicaid access to the people who lost it under those changes.
key_provisions: Remove the requirement that some Medicaid recipients work or volunteer to keep coverage
Restore Medicaid access for certain immigrants who were cut off
Undo new limits on how states can fund their Medicaid programs
who_it_affects: This bill would affect low-income Americans who rely on Medicaid for health insurance, including working-age adults in the Medicaid expansion program and certain immigrants who were recently made ineligible for coverage.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in the House and has been sent to two committees for review, but it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Boat Loan Interest Deduction Act of 2026
plain_title: Tax Break for People Who Take Out Loans to Buy Boats
plain_summary: This bill would allow people to deduct the interest they pay on boat loans from their federal taxes, similar to how homeowners can deduct mortgage interest. For example, if someone borrowed money to buy a boat and paid $2,000 in interest that year, they could use that to lower how much they owe in taxes. Essentially, the government would be giving a financial reward to people who finance boat purchases.
key_provisions: Allow boat loan interest to be tax-deductible
Likely mirrors existing home mortgage interest deduction rules
Reduces taxable income for boat loan borrowers
who_it_affects: This bill would benefit people who take out loans to buy boats, particularly middle- to upper-income individuals who can afford boats and itemize their tax deductions.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in the House of Representatives and has been sent to the Ways and Means Committee, where it will be reviewed before any vote can happen.

original_title: No Goodwill for Harming Women Act
plain_title: No Tax Breaks for Companies That Harm Women
plain_summary: This bill would take away special tax benefits from organizations like Goodwill if they are found to be mistreating or exploiting women. Basically, if a company or nonprofit is caught harming women — such as through unfair wages, unsafe conditions, or abuse — they could lose the financial perks they normally get from the government. It's meant to hold businesses accountable by hitting them where it hurts: their taxes.
key_provisions: Remove tax-exempt status from organizations that harm women
Hold businesses financially accountable for mistreating women
Create consequences for companies that exploit female workers
who_it_affects: This bill would impact nonprofits and businesses — like thrift store chains — that may be underpaying or mistreating women workers, as well as the women who work for those organizations.
status_plain_english: This bill was just introduced in the House and has been sent to a committee to review it — it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe Project Lands Restoration Act
plain_title: Giving Land Back to the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe in Washington
plain_summary: This law gives about 1,083 acres of land in Washington State to the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe, making it officially part of their reservation. When land is taken 'into trust,' the federal government holds it on behalf of the tribe, giving the tribe stronger legal protections over it. However, the tribe is not allowed to build or run a gambling casino on this land.
key_provisions: Over 1,000 acres of Washington land transferred to tribal trust
Land becomes part of the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe's official reservation
Gambling and gaming are banned on the transferred land
who_it_affects: This law directly benefits the Lower Elwha Klallam Tribe by restoring land to their control, while nearby residents and businesses may be affected by new land use rules.
status_plain_english: This bill was fully passed by Congress and signed into law, meaning it is now official U.S. law.

original_title: Tax the Grift Act
plain_title: Taxing Wealthy People Who Profit from Political Power
plain_summary: This bill, called the 'Tax the Grift Act,' appears aimed at taxing money made by politicians or public figures who use their position or fame for personal financial gain. The word 'grift' means making money through dishonest or exploitative means. Because no official summary is available yet, the exact details of how this tax would work are not fully known.
key_provisions: Tax on income earned through political influence or connections
Targeting financial gains seen as improper or corrupt
Details of the tax structure not yet publicly available
who_it_affects: This bill would likely affect politicians, former government officials, or other public figures who earn money by using their public position or fame for personal profit.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and sent to the House Ways and Means Committee, which handles tax-related laws, but it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Honoring the life and legacy of Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson, Sr.
plain_title: Honoring the Life and Legacy of Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr.
plain_summary: This bill is a formal tribute from Congress recognizing the life and contributions of Rev. Jesse Louis Jackson Sr., a major civil rights leader and activist. It honors his decades of work fighting for racial equality, economic justice, and voting rights in America. Bills like this do not create new laws but serve as an official statement of respect from the U.S. government.
key_provisions: Formally recognizes Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr.'s contributions to civil rights
Honors his legacy as an activist, minister, and political figure
Expresses Congress's respect for his life and work
who_it_affects: This bill primarily affects the historical record and public recognition of Rev. Jesse Jackson Sr. and his supporters, as it is a symbolic tribute rather than a law that changes policies.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in the House and has been sent to a committee for review, but has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Reaffirming the commitment of the House of Representatives to preserve and expand pathways to citizenship.
plain_title: Congress Promises to Protect and Create More Ways to Become a Citizen
plain_summary: This bill is a formal statement from the House of Representatives saying they support keeping and creating more ways for people to earn U.S. citizenship. It does not create new laws on its own, but it signals where Congress stands on immigration and citizenship issues. Think of it like a team publicly committing to a goal before deciding the specific plays to make it happen.
key_provisions: Reaffirms support for existing pathways to citizenship
Expresses commitment to expanding new citizenship opportunities
Signals the House's overall position on immigration policy
who_it_affects: This bill would most directly affect immigrants living in the U.S. who are seeking a path to citizenship, as it signals congressional support for protecting and expanding those opportunities.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and sent to the House Judiciary Committee for review, meaning it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Supporting the designation of the week of October 18 through 24, 2026, as "National Chemistry Week".
plain_title: Declaring a National Chemistry Week in October 2026
plain_summary: This bill asks Congress to officially recognize the week of October 18–24, 2026, as 'National Chemistry Week.' It's a symbolic gesture meant to celebrate chemistry and raise public awareness about how important it is in everyday life, from medicines to food to technology. No new laws or funding are created — it's simply an official acknowledgment.
key_provisions: Designates one specific week in October 2026 as National Chemistry Week
Encourages awareness and appreciation of chemistry across the country
Symbolic recognition only — no spending or policy changes required
who_it_affects: This bill would mainly affect students, teachers, and scientists by giving chemistry extra public attention during that week, potentially inspiring schools and organizations to hold chemistry-related events.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and has been sent to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, where members will decide whether to move it forward — it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to modify the rules for investments in qualified opportunity funds, and for other purposes.
plain_title: Changing the Rules for Special Tax-Break Investment Funds
plain_summary: This bill would update tax rules for special investment funds called 'Qualified Opportunity Funds,' which are designed to encourage people to invest money in poorer communities by offering them tax breaks. For example, if someone makes a profit from selling stocks, they can put that money into one of these funds instead of paying taxes on it right away. This bill would change how those tax benefits work to potentially make them more attractive or fair.
key_provisions: Modifying tax benefits for investing in opportunity funds
Changing rules about how long investments must be held
Updating regulations for how these funds operate
who_it_affects: Wealthy investors and businesses who use Qualified Opportunity Funds to reduce their taxes, as well as low-income communities that receive investment through these funds
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in the House of Representatives and has been sent to the Ways and Means Committee, where it will be reviewed before any vote can happen.

original_title: Expressing support for a whole child approach to education and recognizing the role of parents, educators, and community members in providing a whole child approach to education for each student.
plain_title: Supporting a Well-Rounded Education for Every Student
plain_summary: This bill expresses Congress's support for a 'whole child' approach to education, which means schools should focus on students' physical, emotional, social, and academic needs — not just test scores. It recognizes that parents, teachers, and community members all play important roles in helping students thrive. The bill doesn't create new laws or spending, but makes an official statement about how Congress thinks education should work.
key_provisions: Official support for educating the 'whole child,' including health and emotional wellbeing
Recognition that parents, teachers, and communities all share responsibility for student success
Encouragement of schools to meet students' full range of needs beyond just academics
who_it_affects: This bill would symbolically affect students, parents, teachers, and school communities across the U.S. by signaling that Congress values a broader view of student success.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and sent to a House committee for review, meaning it hasn't been voted on yet.

original_title: NO FAKES Act of 2026
plain_title: Protecting People From Fake AI Copies of Themselves
plain_summary: This bill makes it illegal to create or share realistic AI-generated copies of a real person's face or voice without their permission. For example, someone couldn't use AI to make a fake video of a celebrity singing a song or saying something they never said. People whose likenesses are used without permission can sue, and there's a process to get fake content taken down from the internet.
key_provisions: People own the rights to their own voice and face, even after death
Websites must remove unauthorized AI fakes when reported
News reporting, satire, and similar speech are exempt from the rules
who_it_affects: This bill affects everyday people, celebrities, musicians, and actors who could be impersonated by AI, as well as tech companies and content creators who make or share AI-generated content.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and has been sent to a House committee for review, but has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Supporting the designation of the week beginning on October 10, 2026, as "National Wildlife Refuge Week".
plain_title: Declaring a Week to Celebrate National Wildlife Refuges
plain_summary: This bill asks the U.S. government to officially recognize the week of October 10, 2026, as 'National Wildlife Refuge Week.' Wildlife refuges are protected lands set aside for animals and nature, kind of like national parks but focused on wildlife. This recognition would help raise public awareness about these important protected areas across the country.
key_provisions: Officially names the week of October 10, 2026 as National Wildlife Refuge Week
Encourages public awareness and appreciation of wildlife refuges
Supports recognition of the importance of protecting natural habitats for animals
who_it_affects: This bill would affect nature lovers, wildlife conservationists, and anyone who visits or lives near one of the more than 500 national wildlife refuges across the U.S., by drawing attention to these protected natural spaces.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and has been sent to the House Committee on Natural Resources, where lawmakers will decide if it moves forward — it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Unserialized Firearm Harm Oversight and Serialization Act of 2026
plain_title: A Law Requiring Serial Numbers on All Guns
plain_summary: This bill aims to crack down on untraceable firearms, often called 'ghost guns,' which are guns that have no serial numbers and are therefore nearly impossible for police to track. It would require all guns, including homemade or kit-built ones, to have official serial numbers registered with the government. For example, if a ghost gun were used in a crime, law enforcement would now have a better chance of tracing it back to its owner.
key_provisions: Requiring serial numbers on all firearms, including homemade guns
Creating oversight rules to reduce harm caused by unserialized weapons
Likely imposing penalties for owning or making guns without proper serial numbers
who_it_affects: This bill would affect gun owners, gun makers, and law enforcement agencies — gun owners and builders would need to register their weapons, while police would gain better tools to trace guns used in crimes.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in Congress and has been sent to two committees for review, but it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Fire Service Workforce Stability Act of 2026
plain_title: Helping Keep Firefighters Employed and Fire Departments Staffed
plain_summary: This bill aims to make it easier for fire departments to hire and keep firefighters by addressing issues that cause staffing shortages. For example, it may offer financial incentives or reduce barriers that make it hard for fire departments to maintain enough workers. The goal is to make sure communities always have enough firefighters to keep people safe.
key_provisions: financial support or tax benefits for fire departments to maintain staff
measures to help recruit new firefighters into the workforce
protections to help retain experienced firefighters already on the job
who_it_affects: This bill would impact firefighters, fire departments, and the communities they serve by working to ensure fire services remain reliable and fully staffed.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced and has been sent to the House Ways and Means Committee, where lawmakers will review it before deciding whether to move it forward — it has not been voted on yet.

original_title: Protection of Syrian Religious and Ethnic Minorities Act
plain_title: Protecting Religious and Ethnic Minorities in Syria
plain_summary: This bill aims to protect people in Syria who belong to minority religious or ethnic groups, such as Christians, Yazidis, and Kurds, who have faced violence and persecution. It would likely set up ways for the U.S. to help these groups, possibly through aid, refugee protections, or sanctions against those harming them. Because no official summary is available yet, the exact details of how it would do this are still unclear.
key_provisions: Protection measures for Syrian minority groups facing persecution
Possible refugee or immigration relief for at-risk Syrians
Potential financial or foreign policy actions to support minorities
who_it_affects: This bill would most directly impact Syrian religious and ethnic minorities living in Syria or seeking refuge, and could also affect U.S. agencies that handle foreign aid, immigration, and international sanctions.
status_plain_english: This bill was recently introduced in Congress and has been sent to three different committees to review it, but it has not been voted on yet.
